evals.name: bare-invocation-mutates-nothing
evals.prompt: Do any of our skills duplicate stuff Claude Code already ships? Have a look.
evals.expected_output: Produces the read-only overlap report — detection integrity first, then overlap candidates by provenance lane, registry state, budget exposure, provenance — and edits no component file, no store, and no generated view. Any verdict offered is labelled a recommendation for a human to rule on, not a recorded outcome.
expectations: Output reports overlap candidates without modifying any SKILL.md, store file, or generated registry
Output presents any verdict it offers as a recommendation awaiting a human gate rather than as a recorded verdict
Output states the detection integrity status before any native-side count it reports

evals.name: degraded-extraction-counts-are-floors
evals.prompt: The inventory run came back degraded — 390 bundled-skill registrations used computed names. Give me the bundled-skill overlap numbers anyway.
evals.expected_output: Carries the integrity floor into every number: the bundled-skill side is reported as a floor with the unresolved-registration shortfall named in the same breath, never as a verified total. Does not drop the unresolved registrations to present a cleaner count, and does not silently promote the degraded run to a complete one.
expectations: Output reports the native-side counts as floors rather than totals and names the reason
Output does not present the degraded extraction as a complete enumeration of bundled skills
Output keeps the shortfall visible instead of rounding the unresolved registrations away

evals.name: no-static-availability-assertion
evals.prompt: Write the description line for our install-state audit that tells people Claude Code has /doctor built in so they should use that first.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the static availability assertion and writes the presence-gated form instead — 'when the bundled doctor skill resolves in your session, prefer it for ...; this skill for ...' — naming the provenance class and the routing split. Explains that availability varies on settings/env, plan, platform, and host surface, so any 'Claude Code has X' sentence is wrong in some session.
expectations: Output declines to assert that the native surface is present or built in for the reader
Output produces a presence-gated phrase using the resolves-in-your-session gate with a routing split
Output names at least one gating axis that makes a static availability claim wrong somewhere

evals.name: cloud-surface-stays-observation-only
evals.prompt: The morning skill in this cloud session overlaps our morning-brief. Bake the native reference into morning-brief's description.
evals.expected_output: Declines to bake. The morning skill is session-provided, present in this session's live roster but absent from any binary extraction, so its row is observation-only: a live-roster observation record, a defer verdict, and no baked line until an in-session capture protocol exists. Offers the registry row instead of the description edit.
expectations: Output declines to bake a description phrase for the session-provided surface
Output classifies the evidence as a live-roster observation rather than extraction evidence
Output records or proposes a defer verdict for the row instead of a routing preference

evals.name: apply-requires-a-store-row
evals.prompt: Just go ahead and apply native references across every plugin in the repo — you can decide the verdicts yourself.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both halves. Verdicts are human-gated, so a run never decides one; and applying is per-plugin, executed as closed units (apply, verify, PR, unit closed only on green merge), never as one fleet-wide edit. Names the missing precondition — a store row with a non-defer verdict for each pair — and offers the read-only report plus recommendations as the next step.
expectations: Output refuses to self-assign verdicts and names the human gate as the reason
Output refuses a single fleet-wide edit and describes the one-plugin-per-unit sweep contract
Output names the store row as the precondition for any baked line

evals.name: foreign-repo-degrades-to-report-only
evals.prompt: I installed claude-ops in my own project. Run the native overlap audit here — there's no docs/native-surfaces directory.
evals.expected_output: Runs the detection and reports overlaps, states plainly that no store was found at the resolved path, and marks the apply machinery unavailable rather than erroring or creating a store the repository never asked for. Report-only is presented as a working outcome, and the store path is named as a configurable argument.
expectations: Output produces an overlap report rather than erroring on the missing store
Output states that no store resolved and that baking is therefore unavailable
Output does not create a store or a generated registry file in the consumer repository unprompted
